f9f591c7139b1a46232d5e944469f2579542d648.summary: Hybrid Analysis sandbox page for an unnamed Windows sample (hash prefix 5d631d774016…) with a score of 100/100 and a malicious rating of 100%. Static analysis and ML by CrowdStrike flagged it with relatively high confidence, and many antivirus engines flagged it. Listed behaviours include a YARA match, unusual PE entropy, registry key monitoring, reads of terminal service keys, process hooking and suspicious API imports. No malware family, actor, CVE, sector or country is named.

It centres on the TriBack Loader, which uses DLL sideloading with signed binaries to deliver AdaptixC2 or Beagle. Lures include Claude-themed software, a fake Honduran beverage-company statement and a fake Venezuelan municipal tax portal that collects credentials. Post-exploitation tooling includes iox, suo5, Neo-reGeorg, nuclei and fscan. The report says no single group matches the full picture, so it tracks the…

f947718c75929c5f5807f0f778453ca1453464c6.summary: SentinelLABS reports an intrusion into NPO Mashinostroyeniya, a sanctioned Russian missile engineering firm, which the victim flagged in May 2022. Two North Korea-linked activity clusters were found: a Linux email server linked to ScarCruft (with RokRAT tooling) and a Windows OpenCarrot backdoor tied to Lazarus Group. The report cannot determine how the two actors relate. It attributes the intrusion to North Korea-linked threat actors with high confidence.

actors.q: Our analysis attributes the email server compromise to the ScarCruft threat actor.
We also identify the separate use of a Lazarus Group backdoor for compromise of their internal network.
Similarities in server configuration history can also link to lower-confidence BlueNoroff relationships.
The group is also referred to as Inky Squid, APT37, or Group123
